content.text:
Reading the structure from left to right:

- Phenyl ring, then CH2, then CH=CH (drawn trans), attached to pyridine C4.
- Pyridine: N1, C2 bearing the carboxamide, C3 (H), C4 bearing the styryl-type chain, C5 bearing OMe, C6 (H).
- Amide: C(=O)NH-CH2-aryl. The aryl is a meta-disubstituted benzene, with CH2C(=O)N(CH3) on the other position.
- Chain on the N-methyl nitrogen: CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-CH2CH2-O-, counted as four O atoms (three ether Os between ethylene units, plus the terminal aryl ether O).
- The terminal O is attached to C5 of the isoindoline-1,3-dione, whose N carries the 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

Trans alkene: the chain is pyridine-C4–CH=CH–CH2–Ph. Written as SMILES, this is c1(/C=C/Cc2ccccc2).

Assembled SMILES:
COc1cnc(cc1/C=C/Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)NCc1cccc(c1)CC(=O)N(C)CCOCCOCCOCCOc1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1

Checks:
- Pyridine: c1 (C5, OMe), c (C6-H), n, c (C2, amide), c (C3-H), c1 (C4, alkene). This closes the ring correctly.
- Isoindoline: Oc1ccc2C(=O)N(...)C(=O)c2c1. The attachment carbon is c1, then cc, then c2 (bearing C=O), and the ring closes through c2c1. The substituent sits at position 5, which is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cnc(cc1/C=C/Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)NCc1cccc(c1)CC(=O)N(C)CCOCCOCCOCCOc1ccc2C(=O)N(C3CCC(=O)NC3=O)C(=O)c2c1
